blocks.learningGoal: Explain how titration finds an accurate reacting volume and distinguish the practical and calculation pathways.

content.centralQuestion: How can we measure the exact volume needed for neutralisation?
objectives: Set up and use a pipette, burette and conical flask safely
select concordant titres and calculate a mean
Use titration results to calculate an unknown concentration

blocks.learningGoal: Carry out a valid acid–alkali titration and obtain repeatable titres.

sequence: rinse and fill the burette with titrant, then remove the funnel
transfer a fixed aliquot with a volumetric pipette and pipette filler
add two or three drops of a suitable indicator
perform a rough titration, then repeat accurately
near the endpoint add titrant dropwise while swirling
record initial and final readings and calculate each titre
content.safety: Wear eye protection; use a pipette filler; rinse splashes with plenty of water.

blocks.learningGoal: Recognise a scientifically plausible titration arrangement and a faint permanent endpoint.

content.representation: premium realistic burette, clamp, conical flask and white-tile setup
content.accessibleEquivalent: The caption and adjacent method list state every assessed apparatus and endpoint detail.

blocks.learningGoal: Select concordant accurate titres and calculate their mean without using the rough result.

content.guardrail: Use only concordant accurate titres; apply the tolerance stated in the question or centre method.

blocks.learningGoal: Explain why key titration decisions improve accuracy.

decisions: remove the funnel so extra drops cannot change the burette reading
use a white tile to see the endpoint clearly
wash flask walls with distilled water without changing the reacting moles
read the bottom of the meniscus at eye level to avoid parallax

blocks.learningGoal: Use concentration, volume and equation ratio to calculate an unknown concentration.

content.known: 23.60 cm3 of 0.100 mol/dm3 HCl neutralises 25.00 cm3 NaOH

blocks.learningGoal: Demonstrate secure method, data handling and titration-calculation reasoning.

diagnostic.stem: Identify the apparatus that delivers a fixed aliquot.
Calculate a titre from initial and final burette readings.
Explain the purpose of a suitable indicator.

guided.stem: Select concordant titres and calculate a mean.
Calculate an unknown concentration for a 1:1 reaction.

independent.stem: Identify why the funnel is removed.
Explain why distilled water may wash down the flask walls.
Identify and correct a parallax error.
Calculate an unknown concentration using a 2:1 ratio.

exit.stem: State which titres should be included in a mean.
